analysis.title: TSMC (2330.TW) Earnings preview: Strong growth momentum into 2027; CapEx stepping up to support long-term demand; reiterate Buy; TP up to NT$3,300
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on TSMC and raises the 12m price target to NT$3,300 from NT$3,100 (28.2% upside to NT$2,575). The ADR (TSM) target rises to $660 from $620 (39.6% upside to $472.78).
TSMC hosts its 3Q26 analyst meeting on 15 October. GS expects a strong finish to 2026 and a sustained growth outlook into 2027 as demand broadens across AI GPUs, AI ASICs, networking and server CPUs.
Stronger server CPU demand driven by agentic AI is named as the key change over the past year.
GS forecasts USD revenue growth of 42.0% in 2026E and 36.9% in 2027E (2027E was 32.0% previously), with gross margin of 67.2% and 67.5%.
3Q26E revenue is forecast to grow 15.3% QoQ and 4Q26E a further 11.0% QoQ in USD terms, supported by AI/HPC demand.
GS models gross margin at 67.5% in 3Q26E and 67.3% in 4Q26E vs 67.7% in 2Q26, reflecting dilution from the N2 ramp. The N2 dilution is now seen as milder than before.

2027E/2028E CapEx forecasts rise to US$85bn/US$98bn from US$78bn/US$82bn, reflecting equipment vendor cost inflation and initial spending on a potential new Texas expansion. The Texas site is expected to enter mass production only beyond 2032. 2026E CapEx is unchanged at US$64bn.
GS models end-2027E/2028E N3 capacity at 200kwpm/220kwpm and N2 capacity at 140kwpm/200kwpm.
Management at the GS Communacopia + Technology conference said lower token costs should stimulate more AI consumption. Management expects N2 and N3 supply to remain insufficient despite expansion.
Gross margin in 2027E is supported by higher pricing, favorable product mix, sustained high utilization and productivity gains.
GS raises 2026/27/28E EPS by 1%/7%/8% on higher gross margin assumptions (milder N2 dilution) and higher utilization rates for N2/N3.

The target price applies an unchanged 22x P/E to 2027E EPS of NT$150.00. 22x is 1.0 standard deviation above the 5-year average forward P/E and matches TSMC's average during its prior upcycle (2019-2021 revenue CAGR of 28%, vs GS's 38% for 2025-2028E).

Key topics GS wants addressed at the analyst meeting: the AI outlook through 2030, the longer-term CapEx path and US expansion beyond Arizona, and competition from Intel, Samsung and Terafab, including whether the technology lead widens or narrows.
CoWoS advanced packaging capacity is forecast to grow to 1,275k wafers in 2026E, 2,730k in 2027E and 3,480k in 2028E. Shipments are forecast at 1,197k, 2,567k and 3,306k wafers.
GS sees TSMC achieving its 25% revenue CAGR target for the next several years, with long-term gross margin at 56%+, and calls TSMC the key AI enabler in its Taiwan semis coverage.

market_movers.rationale: ADR target raised from $620 on higher 2027E EPS, using 22x P/E, USD/TWD of 30.0 and a 20% ADR premium. Implies 39.6% upside.

sector_views.rationale: AI demand is broadening across accelerators, ASICs, networking and server CPUs, and TSMC holds more than 60% of foundry revenue share with leading-edge supply tight.

earnings_insights: 3Q26E (GS estimate, not yet reported): revenue NT$1,482,698mn, +15.3% QoQ in USD terms, gross margin 67.5%, EPS NT$29.07 (prior GS est NT$28.06).
4Q26E (GS estimate): revenue NT$1,645,937mn, +11.0% QoQ in USD terms, gross margin 67.3%, EPS NT$32.38 (prior GS est NT$31.82).
2Q26 reported (as stated in GS tables): revenue NT$1,270,380mn, gross margin 67.7%, EPS NT$27.25. 1Q26 reported EPS NT$22.08.

FY2026E (GS estimate): EPS NT$110.77 (prior NT$109.21), revenue NT$5,533,119mn. FY2027E (GS estimate): EPS NT$150.00 (prior NT$140.91), revenue NT$7,616,958mn. FY2028E (GS estimate): EPS NT$195.67 (prior NT$180.83).
FY2025 reported EPS NT$66.26 on revenue of NT$3,809,054mn. GS estimates 2026E EPS growth of 67.2% and 2027E of 35.4%.
GS estimates EBIT margin of 59.9% in 2026E and 61.0% in 2027E, and net margin of 51.9% and 51.1%.
The 3Q26 analyst meeting is on 15 October 2026.

trade_ideas.description: Long TSMC (2330.TW) / TSM ADR, Buy rating, 12m target NT$3,300 / $660
trade_ideas.rationale: AI/HPC demand is broadening, N2/N3 supply is tight, and estimates are being revised up.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker end-demand hurting utilization, slower node migrations, a slowdown in AI investment, poor yields, stronger competition or adverse FX.

risk_factors: Further deterioration in end-demand recovery impacting capacity utilization.
Slowdown in AI investment resulting in lower long-term semiconductor content growth.
Poor yields or execution resulting in worse-than-expected profitability.
Stronger competition resulting in ASP and profitability erosion.
Unfavorable FX trend or higher-than-expected cost increases weighing on the margin outlook.
charts_described: Exhibit 4 shows GS CapEx forecasts of US$64bn/85bn/98bn for 2026E/27E/28E vs old forecasts of US$64bn/78bn/82bn.
Exhibit 5 shows annual CoWoS capacity of 144k wafers in 2023 rising to 3,480k in 2028E, with 1,275k in 2026E and 2,730k in 2027E.
geopolitical: Potential new TSMC expansion in Texas, with mass production beyond 2032, and a question of further US expansion beyond the current Arizona site.
